title: Argentinian Parsley and Oregano Chimichurri
summary: Hand-chopped parsley and garlic with softened dried oregano and chilli, sharpened with vinegar and loosened with whisked-in olive oil.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
flat-leaf parsley leaves and tender stems

steps.title: Soften the oregano
steps.text: Stir the dried oregano, salt and chilli flakes into the hot water in the small bowl and leave for 5 min. The water rehydrates the herb so it tastes green and fragrant rather than dusty.

steps.title: Chop by hand
steps.text: Chop the parsley very finely with a sharp knife and put it in the medium bowl with the garlic, vinegar and the softened oregano mixture. Hand chopping keeps the herbs in tiny distinct pieces instead of a purée.

steps.title: Whisk in the oil
steps.text: Pour in the olive oil in a slow stream while whisking, then add the pepper. Doing this by hand matters, because high-speed blending can release bitter compounds from extra-virgin oil.

steps.title: Let it meld
steps.text: Leave the sauce at room temperature for at least 30 min. The garlic loses its raw edge and the herbs flavour the oil.

steps.title: Spoon it over
steps.text: Stir well, as the oil rises to the top, and spoon over sliced grilled steak, chicken or charred vegetables.

tips: Making it in a blender is a common mistake; it gives a bitter, muddy paste instead of a bright, loose sauce.
Pat the parsley dry before chopping so the knife cuts cleanly instead of bruising it.
Add a little more chilli if you like it hot, but keep the parsley in charge.
Made a day ahead, the flavour gets deeper but the colour dulls slightly.
storage: Keep covered in the fridge for up to 1 week; let it stand at room temperature 20 min and stir before serving. Freeze in ice-cube trays for up to 3 months. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
